summary_html: **CAPTA §5106a(c)** requires every state to maintain **Citizen Review Panels** that evaluate CPS policies. Project Milk Carton checks whether panels are active, independent, and publicly reporting.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: In a systemic challenge to Florida's foster care system, standing must be shown claim by claim; some plaintiffs' claims were moot and others were dismissed for lack of standing, leaving only counts for which a particular plaintiff demonstrated injury in fact.
key_cases.relevance: Bush marks the boundary between citizen oversight mechanisms and judicially cognizable claims.
key_cases.quote: Only Reggie B. has standing to pursue the procedural due process claims set out in Count II, because he is the only plaintiff who has demonstrated injury in fact

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The 'reasonable efforts' requirement of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act creates no privately enforceable right, so beneficiaries could not sue state child welfare officials under section 1983 to enforce it.
key_cases.relevance: Citizen review panels and similar bodies operate as substitutes for judicially enforceable rights under the Act.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: In re Records of the Department of Children & Family Services (Sarasota Herald-Tribune v. Department of Children & Family Services)
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, Second District
key_cases.holding: A circuit court considering a petition for access to confidential child abuse records must conduct an in camera review before ruling; refusing to inspect the records was an abuse of discretion and the denial of access was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: Independent review of agency performance depends on this in camera mechanism for reaching otherwise confidential files.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court abused its discretion when it failed to conduct an in camera review of the records to which the Herald-Tribune seeks access
